SellKit User Onboarding and Guide

The operating guide for Mariah Rubino: sign in, complete setup, review the Signal Radar, test ICPs quickly, work the scored queue with buying-committee context, approve manual outreach drafts, track conversions by hand, and let the dashboard learn which signals and personas actually convert. Nothing sends automatically.

Audience: Mariah Rubino Mode: manual-first Generated: Jun 12, 2026, 2:15 PM

What SellKit Does

SellKit helps Mariah review account and buyer recommendations before outreach. One page combines six surfaces:

  • Signal Radar: fresh account signals (new leadership, hiring spikes, cloud efficiency pressure) waiting for a Review / Add to queue / Ignore decision.
  • ICP Preview Lab: type an ICP and test it with a fast lookup or a capped 10-match preview before a broader list build.
  • Review queue: scored targets with signal evidence, a five-seat buying committee map, and draft copy.
  • Enrichment gate: Apollo work-email enrichment unlocks only at score 75+, by manual click, with a visible batch cap.
  • Manual handoff: approved drafts become copyable email text, a downloadable .eml, and a CRM CSV. Nothing is sent or written for you.
  • Conversion learning: tracked outcomes roll up into signal-level and persona-level rates, and the Signal Discovery Agent suggests new signals to test each week.
No automatic send. SellKit prepares drafts and exports. Mariah reviews and approves before anything is copied, downloaded, or imported elsewhere. No email, LinkedIn, Salesforce, or enrichment runs without a click.

Before First Use

  • Use the approved work account to sign in.
  • Confirm that external sourcing and enrichment tools are allowed under company policy.
  • Keep provider keys server-side. Do not paste API keys into the browser or guide.
  • Use manual email, manual CRM import, and manual LinkedIn steps until Microsoft, Salesforce, or LinkedIn access is approved.

First-Time Onboarding

The onboarding panel opens automatically until all five questions are answered (use Edit Onboarding to reopen it later). Answer the questions, then click Save Progress — answers save to the signed-in account and restore on any browser. The goal is not a perfect spec. The goal is enough context for SellKit to recognize the right big-tech account, the right executive buyer, the right trigger, and the right expert-services angle.

1 Ideal target company Describe the account where outside experts would be credible and timely. v

What to say

Use size, maturity, function, geography, and transformation context. For expert services, fit is usually about urgency plus complexity, not just industry.

Big tech Enterprise SaaS AI platform rollout Cloud migration Post-reorg execution

Example answer

Enterprise software or big-tech teams with 2,000+ employees, US first, active platform, AI, data, cloud, or product operating model initiatives. Avoid small startups unless they just hired a senior transformation leader.

Good SellKit input: "Large engineering/product orgs dealing with AI adoption, platform modernization, cloud efficiency pressure, or post-reorg change. Prioritize teams that would value former Google, HP, MongoDB, or enterprise SaaS operators."
2 Buyer titles Name who can feel the pain, sponsor the work, or bring in expert help. v

Strong yes titles

CTO, CIO, VP Engineering, VP Product, Head of Platform, Head of Data/AI, Chief Transformation Officer, GM, Product Ops, Engineering Enablement, or Strategy/Ops leaders attached to product and engineering.

Close but no

Recruiting-only titles, junior program managers, vendor management without business ownership, or people too far from the change initiative.

Good SellKit input: "Prioritize VP+ Product, Engineering, Data/AI, Platform, CIO/CTO, Transformation, and Product Ops. Avoid recruiters and junior PMO unless they report directly into a named transformation program."
3 One-line offer Make the service concrete: who the experts are and what business problem they help with. v

Offer patterns

Change management consultants, former product/engineering executives, domain experts, or fractional operators who help teams make a difficult initiative real.

AI adoption Dev productivity Product operating model Platform scale Cloud efficiency

Example answer

We connect enterprise product and engineering teams with proven operators and domain experts for urgent transformation work, from AI rollout and platform modernization to change management and executive advisory.

Avoid vague offers: "Expert network access" is too generic. Better: "former product, engineering, AI, and change leaders who can help your team de-risk a specific initiative."
4 Buying signals Rank the events that make expert help timely, not merely interesting. v

High-intent triggers

New CTO/CIO/VP Eng, major reorg, AI platform launch, hiring spike for platform/data/product ops, cloud efficiency initiative, acquisition integration, enterprise transformation program, or public roadmap shift.

What good looks like

A visible initiative plus an owner. Example: "new VP Engineering hired in the last 90 days and the company is hiring platform productivity leaders."

Good SellKit input: "Strongest signals: new product/engineering leadership, AI/data platform rollout, change management after reorg, cloud or infra efficiency pressure, and senior hiring for platform/product ops."
5 Email voice Give SellKit a real tone to imitate: direct, credible, and tied to the signal. v

What to provide

One or two real emails, preferred subject length, whether to mention the signal, and how direct the ask should be.

Example opener

"Saw your platform org is hiring around developer productivity after the AI infra rollout. We help teams bring in former product and engineering operators who have led similar transitions."

Good SellKit input: "Short, plain, low-hype. Mention the specific signal in sentence one. Offer a useful expert angle, not a broad pitch. Ask for a quick compare-notes conversation."

Daily Workflow

  1. Sign in: open SellKit and authenticate with the approved account.
  2. Sweep the Signal Radar: review fresh account signals. Add the timely ones to the queue, ignore the noise. Ignored signals can be reconsidered later.
  3. Review the queue: pick the highest-scored target and inspect the company, title, signal, and email confidence.
  4. Read evidence and the committee: open source links where needed; identify the primary buyer, champion, blocker, budget holder, and technical evaluator. Refresh committee map re-researches on demand — by click only.
  5. Enrich selectively: if the target clears the score gate (75+) and you need a verified work email, click Enrich work email. The batch counter shows how much of the 10-target cap is used.
  6. Approve only when ready: approve the draft after reviewing copy. Approval unlocks copy/download of the manual email and the CRM CSV export.
  7. Track what happens: after sending manually, click Track sent, then Track reply / meeting / won as outcomes arrive. Tracked targets stay in the CRM export.
  8. Read the dashboard weekly: conversion learning shows which signals and personas convert; Signal Discovery suggests the next signals to test.

Signal Radar

The radar is the top of the funnel: each card is one account signal with its type, provider, detected date, why it matters, suggested buyer persona, and a confidence tier.

  • Review marks a signal as seen without acting on it.
  • Add to queue promotes the account toward the review queue. This is the only path from radar to outreach, and it is always a manual click.
  • Ignore parks the signal. Ignored signals can be re-reviewed if circumstances change.

Radar decisions save to Mariah's account. No outreach, enrichment, or provider action ever starts from this surface.

ICP Preview Lab

Use the lab to tune targeting criteria before a broader list build. Describe the ICP in plain language and pick a mode:

  • Fast lookup (Parallel Entity Search): instant candidate set for quick gut checks.
  • Preview run (Parallel FindAll Preview): up to 10 sample matches with match reasons. A full FindAll run never starts from here.

Each match shows the company, match reason, provider, and confidence, with an Add to Signal Radar action. If the provider is unavailable, SellKit shows a clearly-labeled sample set.

Enrichment Gate, Tracking, and Export

Apollo enrichment is score-gated

  • Blocked below a composite score of 75. The card shows the current score, the threshold, and why a target is blocked.
  • Manual click only, work email only — no phone or personal email enrichment.
  • A visible batch counter enforces the 10-target cap. Rejected and suppressed targets stay blocked regardless of score.

Track conversions by hand

After approving and manually sending, record what happened with Track sent, Track reply, Track meeting, and Track won. Tracking is for reporting only — it never triggers a send, LinkedIn action, or CRM write. Events save to Mariah's account and survive reloads.

CRM CSV export

  • The export includes every approved target, including targets whose status has advanced (sent, replied, meeting, won). Lost and suppressed targets are excluded.
  • Cells that start with =, +, -, or @ are neutralized so provider-supplied text cannot execute as a spreadsheet formula when the file opens in Excel or Google Sheets.
  • Import the CSV into the CRM manually after policy review.

Conversion Learning and Signal Discovery

Everything Mariah tracks feeds the dashboard:

  • Signal-level conversion: approval, reply, positive reply, meeting, and win rates per signal — e.g. how "new data leader" replies compare with "hiring spike" meetings.
  • Persona performance: the same rates across CTO, VP Engineering, VP Data, Head of Transformation, and Security/CISO buyers.
  • Signal Discovery Agent: a weekly recommendation queue computed from converted-versus-ignored history — e.g. "platform hiring + AI observability language converted 2.4x better than funding-only accounts" — with evidence, a lift estimate, sample accounts, and an Add to radar criteria action. It recommends; it never reaches out.

Provider Roles and API Appendix

Use the providers as stages in one workflow, not as substitutes for each other. This table is for operating SellKit after Mariah understands the basic review flow.

Stage Best Provider Use It For Guardrail
Account discovery Exa Company Search ICP-matched company lists by industry, headcount, geography, funding stage, and technology. Use the company category, request highlights, and store structured company metadata separately from evidence snippets.
Buyer discovery Exa People Search Likely buyers, senior leaders, profile URLs, current role, location, and career context. Run 2-3 query variations, dedupe by profile URL/name/company, and do not treat Exa as verified email.
Interactive lookup Parallel Entity Search Fast people/company results when Mariah types a natural-language search. Use for candidate sets only. It is fast, but not a cited enrichment run.
ICP test Parallel FindAll Preview Quickly evaluate about 10 candidates before a broader list build. Always preview first, read matched and unmatched candidates, then adjust match conditions.
Deep list-building Parallel FindAll or Exa Websets Verified account/person lists with reasoning, citations, enrichments, webhooks, and async completion. Cap match limits, use webhooks for longer jobs, and only enrich matched candidates.
Account dossier Exa Agent or Parallel Task Buying committee maps, why-now research, recent initiatives, objections, and structured talking points. Use bounded JSON schemas and require source URLs for every important claim.
Contact enrichment Apollo Verified work email, firmographic validation, and selective people/company enrichment after scoring. Blocked below composite score 75; the in-app gate enforces it. Manual click only, batch cap of 10, work email only — no phone or personal email.
Fallback review Clay Spreadsheet-style human enrichment queues and ambiguous rows that need manual review. Test one row first, store credentials in Clay connections, set rate limits, and return only needed fields.

API Best Practices

Evidence-First Scoring

Every score component should be traceable. Store the provider, source URL, source title, source date, retrieval time, excerpt, confidence, and why the evidence matters.

  • Signal strength: link to a press release, hiring page, earnings note, product post, or funding source.
  • Title fit: link to the profile or public bio used to identify the buyer.
  • Company fit: link to Exa company metadata or the source supporting headcount, industry, funding, or tech stack.
  • Email confidence: show Apollo status separately from the score and keep raw enrichment output server-side.

Usage Controls

  • Debounce interactive searches and cache provider responses by normalized query.
  • Use Parallel Entity Search for quick lookups and FindAll Preview before full FindAll runs.
  • Cap Exa Agent, Exa Websets, and Parallel FindAll list sizes before running.
  • Use Apollo only after a target passes score thresholds. Bulk enrich in batches of 10.
  • Do not enrich phone numbers or personal emails unless explicitly approved.

Compliance Defaults

  • No automatic send. SellKit prepares copy, .eml files, and exports only after approval.
  • No automatic LinkedIn action. SellKit can prepare a note and profile link for manual use.
  • Keep all API keys server-side and never expose them in browser requests, screenshots, or exports.
  • Keep raw provider payloads separate from normalized app rows so data can be audited or deleted.
  • Use work email before personal email. Treat phone enrichment as disabled unless Mariah explicitly opts in.
  • CSV exports neutralize leading =, +, -, @ so provider text cannot execute as a spreadsheet formula.
  • Provider/agent output is length-clamped and URL-validated before display; it can never override the manual-first guardrails.

Provider References

  • Exa Company Search - company discovery and structured company metadata.
  • Exa People Search - professional profiles and buyer discovery.
  • Exa Agent - deep research, grounded structured JSON, and account dossiers.
  • Exa Websets - verified async list-building and enrichment.
  • Parallel Entity Search - fast synchronous people and company lookup.
  • Parallel FindAll Preview - quick validation before full FindAll runs.
  • Parallel FindAll - cited, verified, enriched list-building.
  • Apollo People Enrichment - verified contact enrichment after scoring.
  • Clay HTTP API and Clay Webhooks - manual enrichment workspace and row handoff.

Troubleshooting

  • Login loop: sign out, reopen the SellKit URL, and use the approved account.
  • Copy is disabled: approve the draft first. Copy/download stays disabled before approval.
  • CRM export is not ready: approve at least one target. Targets you have tracked (sent, replied, meeting, won) remain in the export.
  • Track buttons are disabled: approve the draft first; each event can only be tracked once per target.
  • Enrich work email is blocked: the target is below the 75-score threshold, already enriched, rejected/suppressed, or the 10-target batch cap is used up. The card states the reason.
  • Radar or preview shows sample data: the provider was unavailable; the labeled fallback keeps the workflow moving. Try again later for live results.
  • Draft sounds wrong: update the onboarding email voice field with a real example and Save Progress.
  • Score seems unclear: inspect Evidence-First Scoring and source links before approving.
Policy reminder. Keep the app manual-first until company policy approves direct Microsoft, Salesforce, or LinkedIn integrations.
